Synopsis:
Australia's newly established National Environmental Protection Agency has approved its first coal project — an extension of BHP Mitsubishi Alliance's Saraji open-cut metallurgical coal mine in Queensland — permitting extraction of an additional 55Mt of coal through 2055. The approval includes habitat clearance conditions for several threatened species. The decision draws sharp criticism from climate groups and sits in tension with Prime Minister Albanese's climate rhetoric at the Pacific Islands Forum. Critics highlight incompatibility with IEA net-zero pathways and Australia's safeguard mechanism, which notably excludes Scope 3 (overseas combustion) emissions.
